The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress in Rivers State, Gabriel Pidomson, has promised to create between 50,000 and 100,000 jobs in the state through agriculture if elected governor in 2027. Pidomson said the plan would involve providing young people with farmland, start-up loans, agricultural training and access to markets for their produce. He spoke during a programme aired on Wazobia FM in Port Harcourt on Friday, monitored by our correspondent. The governorship hopeful said the state had enough fertile land and water resources to support large-scale farming and reduce its dependence on imported food. According to him, the agricultural programme would focus on fish, shrimp and crab farming in riverine communities, while cassava, maize, vegetables, rice, palm oil and poultry production would be developed in other parts of the state. The fact is that we want to employ at least 50,00 to 100,000 young people.” Utilise skills acquired during orientation, Rivers NYSC coordinator urges corps members 2027: Group drums up support for Tinubu, Ododo in Kogi Don’t attack defectors, Obidient coordinator warns supporters The plan, he said, also includes establishing agro-processing centres to turn farm produce such as cassava into garri and starch, as well as processed rice, palm oil, fish and poultry products for local consumption and export. Pidomson further promised to establish what he described as the largest fish farm east of the Niger to boost production and create more jobs. The state ADC governorship candidate expressed optimism that the agricultural programme would also develop rural communities, reduce migration to the city and create employment opportunities beyond Port Harcourt, the state capital. He added, “We will establish the largest fish farm in the East of the Niger. It will be a mega fish estate that will have different types of fish to be located in the Kalabari axis of the state. “With such an industry there, people will not need to come to Port Harcourt again. “It means people who don’t have jobs and want to run to Port Harcourt for jobs and possibly add to the challenge of insecurity will now be going to work from their houses there.” Dennis Naku Dennis Naku is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with approximately 19 years of professional experience.
